learning_outcomes.text: Evaluates the economic aspects of product development.
Performs the life cycle analysis. Evaluates the environmental and sustainability consequences of different industrial projects.
Applies the legal framework in the execution and implementation of projects.
Prepares preliminary projects within their specialty.
Knows the scope of action and limitations of industrial technical engineering in mechanics.
Applies knowledge of business organization and production management.
Organizes and manages projects. Knows the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Defines the tasks to achieve project objectives. Plans implementation monitoring mechanisms. Identifies potential inherent project risks. Establishes clear project objectives.
Forecasts and allocates necessary times to complete planned actions. Plans an evaluation of project results. Monitors project implementation.

Recognizes ethical and deontological concepts of the area of knowledge, shows critical and dialogue capacity, and makes responsible use of the norms that affect them as a member of the university community. (Ethics)

Identifies the main environmental problems. (Environment) Recognizes and reflects on social needs and problems and gets involved in community improvement. (Social responsibility as a citizen and professional)

syllabus_topics: The engineer and their attributions. Basic aspects of engineering projects
Methodology and formulation: Definition of objectives. Study of constraints. Study of alternatives. Process engineering. Installation engineering.
Project morphology: Report. Plans. Specifications. Budget.
Project evaluation: Economic and financial evaluation. Environmental evaluation.
Project development: Processing. Contracting. Executive and environmental management.
Monitoring and control: Time planning. Resource management.

Preparation of technical reports: Expert opinions, Safety studies in works, Technical Building Code: Structural Safety, Fire Safety, Usability Safety, Salubrity and Energy Saving, RITE, ITE (Technical Building Inspection)

Practices: Structuring of project documents (Application of standards), Technical reports, Calculation of elements and installations (computer management), Financial evaluation (computer management), Project scheduling, Measurements and budgets (computer management)
teaching_methods: Problem-solving/exercises in the ordinary classroom (Resolution of problems and exercises in the classroom for application of theory)
ICT practices in computer labs (Preparation of reports and partial works for project documents)
Preliminary project (Preparation of a preliminary project, as group work)
Personalized attention (Students will have personalized attention during consultation hours)
assessment_rules: All practices are compulsory and not recoverable. To average the different parts, a minimum grade must be achieved in all parts. If any part does not reach the minimum grade, the course will be failed. For the second and additional calls, the same structure and weightings will be maintained, but practice grades will be those obtained in the first call as they are not recoverable until the next academic year. The minimum grade for each part to be averaged and their specific weights are established at the beginning of the course by the professor.
